newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index up to 600-points on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index up to 600-points on foreign buying.

text.p: The Jakarta share index crossed the key resistance level of 600-points at closing on Thursday on the back of selective foreign buying of some big and medium-sized stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.42 points, or 0.91 percent to close at 600.91 points. Gainers led losers by 59 to 53, with 60 counters unchanged.
"If foreigners continue buying some big-capitalised stock, I believe it will support the index at around the 600-point level on Friday and lend a positive tone to the market," a foreign broker said.
"Some foreign investors have started to trade based on 1997 price earnings because there are only two months left in 1996," an analyst of Japanese brokerage firm said.
Brokers said some foreign buyers had re-entered the market in late trading and targetting blue chip stocks including Astra, Gudang Garam, Telkom and Semen Gresik.

Vehicle manufacturer Astra International rose 3.75 percent, from 4,000 rupiah to 4,150 rupiah on a turnover of 866,000 shares. Brokers said it was due to fresh-buying on its fundamentals after an analysts briefing on Wednesday on its nine-month results.

"Aside from recent speculation on the ownership in Astra, it is an attractive stock and has good long term prospects. It has a huge hidden value in its subsidaries," analyst of major local brokerage firm said.
The country's largest retail firm Matahari was also actively traded with 2.1 million shares changing hands, up 100 rupiah to 2,450 rupiah on fresh buying.
Brokers said some investors picked up the stocks from the market on its prospects, also boosted by company's commitment to slowing down its expansion.
Cement maker Semen Gresik was targeted by foreign buying on after an analysts report said the expected oversupply of cement would be in the year of 2000 rather than 1998 as expected.
It rose 150 rupiah to 7,625 rupiah on a turnover 732,500 shares.

"As Indonesia's largest cement producer next year and with its subsidiaries holding the only cement export licences, Gresik is best positioned to respond to either an upturn or downturn in demand," Asia Equity Indonesia said in the report.
Bank International Indonesia rose 125 rupiah to 2,150 rupiah on 5.9 million shares.
Brokers attributed the movement to fresh buying on its fundamentals coupled with a spinoff effect from BNI's well-received public offer last week.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia was also actively traded on its fundamentals. It rose 50 rupiah to 2,600 rupiah on a turnover of 4.2 million shares.
